### Phase 7D — Payroll Master-Data Integrity & Payroll Entry UI Refinements — IMPLEMENTED, 2026-07-30, awaiting review, NOT COMMITTED

A production UAT checkpoint, not a new roadmap phase in `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`'s numbering —
closes a defect class discovered during authenticated production use of the Payroll Entry grid.

**Master data boundary audit (repository evidence, before any change).** `PayrollEntry` (schema)
duplicated five `Employee` columns as its own — `designation`, `bankId`, `branchCode`,
`accountNumber`, `iban` — copied at entry-creation/cycle-bootstrap time, then independently
Draft-editable via the ordinary `PATCH /payroll-entries/:id` route
(`updatePayrollEntrySchema`/`mapUpdateInputToEntryData`), with none of `employees.service.ts`'s own
uniqueness/banking-invariant validation applied at that write path. `employeeNameSnapshot`/
`fatherNameSnapshot` are a *separate*, deliberate, already-correct historical-snapshot mechanism
(frozen at creation, read by Payslips/Bank Sheets for historical stability) — not touched by this
checkpoint. `cnic`/`employeeCode` were never duplicated at all — always read live via the `employee`
relation, already correct. `eobiAmount`/`eobiApplicable` are duplicated too, but by explicit design
(a legitimate payroll-cycle-specific toggle) — this checkpoint's classification: **A. Employee master
data** = designation/bankId/branchCode/accountNumber/iban/name/fatherName/cnic/employeeCode;
**B. Payroll-cycle transaction data** = cycle days/hours/rates/leave/allowance/advances/fine/hold/
remarks/eobiAmount/eobiApplicable; **C. Historical payroll snapshot data** = the entry's own frozen
columns once released, and `employeeNameSnapshot`/`fatherNameSnapshot` always.

**Fix — Employee Registry as sole authoritative, editable source (Part 1).**
`shared/src/schemas/payroll-entry.ts`'s `updatePayrollEntrySchema` no longer declares
`designation`/`bankId`/`branchCode`/`accountNumber`/`iban` at all (Zod strips unrecognized keys by
default — a PATCH still sending them has them silently ignored, verified by a dedicated test rather
than assumed). `payroll-entry.service.ts` gains `withLiveMasterData()`: for any entry with
`released = false` and `payoutOutcome = null`, it overwrites those five stored columns with the
*live* `Employee` record's current values before the response is returned — applied in
`listPayrollEntries`, `getPayrollEntry`, and every mutation's own re-fetch (`updatePayrollEntry`,
`addWorkLine`, `updateWorkLine`, `deleteWorkLine`); each of those queries' `employee` include was
widened to select the five fields. This is display-time only — it never writes back to the entry's
own stored column — so a Draft/Open cycle always reflects Employee Registry after an ordinary
refresh, with zero separate "resync" action, and the entry can never independently drift from it.
`payroll-release.service.ts`'s `releaseProjectUnit` gains the write-time half:
`liveMasterByEntryId`, computed from each release candidate's live `Employee` record *before*
`evaluatePayrollEntryReleaseReadiness` runs (so eligibility itself is checked against current data,
never a stale column), then spread into the `paidIds`/`noPayDueIds`/`recoveryEntries` per-entry
`update()` calls (switched from bulk `updateMany` to per-entry `update`, since each entry's synced
values differ — still bounded by one Unit's own headcount, matching this file's own audit-log loop
immediately below it). This is the moment the entry's stored columns get frozen permanently,
accurate as-of-release rather than as-of-creation — the historical-snapshot guarantee Payslips/Bank
Sheets already rely on (`entry.designation`/`.bankId`/etc., read directly, unaffected by this
checkpoint) now starts from a materially more accurate baseline. `payroll-entry-import-export.
service.ts` was audited and confirmed export-only — no import/mutation path exists for these fields,
nothing to change there.

**EOBI applicability (explicit exception).** Confirmed still fully editable via the ordinary PATCH
route (`eobiAmount`/`eobiApplicable` remain in `updatePayrollEntrySchema`), confirmed functionally
correct in a new dedicated test (toggled off for one cycle without touching Employee Registry's own
default, and a later Employee Registry default change does not silently re-flip an already-set
entry). Never moved to Employee Registry, never made read-only, per this checkpoint's explicit
instruction. **Superseded the same day** — see "Phase 7D refinement — EOBI Bidirectional
Synchronisation," below: the client's own follow-up instruction requires Employee Registry and the
current Draft entry to stay *consistent*, not merely both independently editable, so a Draft-entry
toggle change now also writes back to Employee Registry (and vice versa). `eobiApplicable` remains a
fully Payroll-Entry-editable, never-read-only toggle exactly as this paragraph found; only the
"changes to it never propagate" half of this paragraph's claim no longer holds.

**Frontend (Part 1 cont'd).** `payroll-entry-row.tsx`: `designation`/`bankId`/`branchCode`/
`accountNumber`/`iban` cells changed from `InlineTextCell`/`InlineSelectCell` to `ReadOnlyCell`
(same pattern `employeeCode`/`employeeName` already used), reading `entry.*` directly rather than
`effectiveEntry.*` (no local draft state for these fields any more — `EntryDraft`'s type, derived
from `UpdatePayrollEntryInput`, no longer has them at all). The now-unused `InlineSelectCell` import
was removed. `columns.ts`'s `NAVIGABLE_COLUMN_IDS` (Arrow-key grid navigation) no longer lists these
five ids — nothing focusable remains in those cells to navigate to.

**Totals-row overlap (Part 2).** Root cause confirmed via repository evidence: `computeColumnWidths`
measured every column's width purely from individual body-row values (plus, for
Advance/Eid-Advance, their balance sub-label) — never from the *summed footer total* the totals row
actually displays, which can legitimately be far wider than any single row's value (e.g.
"1,502 employees", or a Gross Pay sum across hundreds of rows). The totals row is deliberately
`overflow-visible`/`whitespace-nowrap` (financial values are never truncated), so a too-narrow
column meant the total visibly overlapped the next column. Fix: `computeColumnWidths` now also
computes each numeric total column's actual summed value from the full loaded dataset (a new
`computeStaticFooterTotals`, reusing `computeServerSnapshot` — the same server-truth snapshot
`LiveTotalsStore` itself seeds from) and the Employee column's "N employees" footer text, formats
each exactly as `PayrollEntryTotalsRow` would (`extractFooterValue`), and feeds that formatted text
into the same `measureColumnWidth` pass column values are already measured against — the identical
technique `BALANCE_LABEL_COLUMN_IDS` already used for the Advance-balance sub-label. `MONEY_TOTAL_
COLUMN_IDS`/`NUMERIC_TOTAL_COLUMN_IDS` are now exported from `columns.ts` and imported by
`payroll-entry-totals-row.tsx` (previously two independently-defined, potentially-drifting copies)
— no duplicated source of truth for "which columns get a summed total" or "which are money-
formatted." No font-size reduction anywhere; no new horizontal scrolling introduced (the fix widens
columns within the grid's own existing measured-width architecture).

**Advance Balance presentation (Part 3).** Root cause: the stacked "amount input + Bal: PKR X" label
block's total content height (`InlineNumberCell`'s `py-1` + the input's own line-height, plus
`BalanceLabel`'s `mt-0.5` + its own line-height) landed almost exactly at the fixed `ROW_HEIGHT`
(40px), leaving no real clearance from the row's own `border-b` — any minor font-metric variance
pushed the balance text flush against/touching the border. Fix: `InlineNumberCell` gained a
`compact` prop (`py-0.5` instead of `py-1`, applied only when a balance label is present, via
`tailwind-merge`-safe `cn()`), and `BalanceLabel` changed `mt-0.5` → `mt-0` plus added
`leading-none` — together shaving enough height to give the two-line block genuine breathing room
inside the unchanged 40px row (`ROW_HEIGHT` itself, and the row's own `items-center` vertical
centering, both untouched). Applied identically to `advanceDeduction` and `eidAdvanceDeduction`; an
advance/eid-advance cell with no linked balance is unaffected (ordinary non-compact padding).
Financial value/calculation completely untouched — presentation only, as required.

**Payslip PDF logo removal (Part 4).** `lib/pdf/templates/payslip.ts`: the `<img>` embed, the local
`PAYSLIP_EXTRA_STYLES` block (`.doc-header-row`/`.doc-header-logo`), and the `companyLogoDataUri`
field on `PayslipPdfMeta` are deleted entirely — the client does not want the logo on Payslips at
all, never a logo, never a placeholder. `.doc-header` now renders `.doc-company-name`/
`.doc-company-detail` directly (no wrapping flex row), relying on the shared `PRINT_STYLES`'s own
`.doc-header { text-align: center; }` — identical centering to before, since the logo was always
capped below the two-line company-name block's own height specifically so it could never affect
`.doc-header`'s height (confirmed via a rewritten geometry-preservation test). `payslips.routes.ts`'s
two call sites (`/pdf` and `/batch`) no longer fetch `getCompanyLogoDataUri()` at all — removed
along with its now-unused import. **Statement PDFs, Bank Sheets, Cash Receiving, Login, Sidebar, and
Company Settings are completely untouched** — confirmed via repository audit that Statement's own
`.doc-header-logo` CSS/embed is an independent, deliberately-uncoupled copy (its own doc comment
says so explicitly), never shared code with Payslip's template; Bank Sheet/Cash Receiving are
ExcelJS/CSV exports with no logo rendering of any kind to begin with.

**A pre-existing test-construction technique became obsolete, and was rewritten rather than left
silently broken.** Four tests — two in `payroll-entry-release-readiness.test.ts`, two in
`payroll-release-eligibility.test.ts` — constructed a "duplicate/missing banking data" release-block
scenario by directly mutating a `PayrollEntry`'s own stored column via raw Prisma (bypassing the app
layer entirely), simulating "the entry's frozen snapshot outlives the employee's own later
correction." That is precisely the stale-duplication defect this checkpoint's architecture change
eliminates for an unreleased entry (display and release-eligibility both now read Employee
Registry's live value, never the entry's own possibly-stale column) — under the new architecture the
old test setup has no effect at all. Two tests were rewritten to construct the equivalent state on
the *Employee* record instead (a direct Prisma write bypassing `employees.service.ts`'s own
`applyBankingInvariant`, which would otherwise reject a bank-with-no-account-number at the ordinary
API boundary — still a genuine defense-in-depth scenario for corrupt data, the same "construct a
state the app itself would never normally produce" pattern already used elsewhere in this suite for
CNIC/Employee-Code duplicates). Two tests were rewritten to explicitly assert the fix itself: a
stale entry column no longer produces a false block, and release/Finalize now succeed cleanly where
they previously (incorrectly, under the old architecture) failed.

**Testing.** New: `payroll-entry-master-data-boundary.test.ts` (backend, 6 tests — live Draft
refresh for banking/designation, EOBI toggle independence, ordinary financial-field editability,
released-entry immutability) and `master-data-boundary.test.tsx` (frontend, 16 tests — read-only
cells render no `<input>`/`<select>`, financial fields and EOBI/Hold toggles remain interactive,
totals-row width widens for large sums/headcounts and stays sane at zero, `ROW_HEIGHT` unchanged,
Advance Balance `compact`/`mt-0`/`leading-none` classes). Updated: `payroll-entry.test.ts` (the old
"banking refinement" PATCH test rewritten to prove PATCH-attempted banking/identity edits are now
silently ignored, both in the response and on disk), `payroll-release.test.ts` (new test proving
release freezes Employee Registry's value *as of release time*, capturing a pre-release correction,
not whatever the entry was bootstrapped with — plus the pre-existing "already-released entry stays
frozen" test re-confirmed unchanged), `pdf-template.test.ts` (Payslip's old three logo-presence
tests replaced with three logo-absence/geometry-preservation tests; Statement's own logo tests
untouched), and the four rewritten eligibility/readiness tests above.

**Results.** Backend: **61 suites / 1195 tests, all passing** — verified via two full sequential
runs against an isolated, freshly-provisioned local PostgreSQL (embedded-postgres, this session's
own scratchpad, migrated + seeded fresh, per `docs/PROJECT_PROGRESS.md`'s existing "Local Postgres

### Phase 7D refinement — EOBI Bidirectional Synchronisation — IMPLEMENTED, 2026-07-30, awaiting review, NOT COMMITTED

A same-day follow-up to the Phase 7D checkpoint above, which had confirmed EOBI applicability stays
Payroll-Entry-editable and *independent* of Employee Registry. The client's own explicit instruction
overrides that: because both screens must stay consistent, a change on either side must now also
write to the other. Employee Registry remains the source of truth for the employee's current/default
value; the current Draft entry may still operate on it operationally, but after any successful
change:

```
Employee.defaultEobiApplicable === current Draft PayrollEntry.eobiApplicable
```

**Design — one shared service function, no recursive calls.** A new module,
`backend/src/modules/payroll-entry/eobi-sync.service.ts`, exports `syncEobiApplicability()` — the
single place either direction's write happens. It has no dependency on `employees.service.ts` or
`payroll-entry.service.ts` (only `prisma`'s transaction type and `audit-log.service.ts`), so both of
those modules can import it with no circular-import risk. `employees.service.ts`'s `updateEmployee`
and `payroll-entry.service.ts`'s `updatePayrollEntry` each call it, once, from inside their own
existing `prisma.$transaction` — never a second, independent transaction, never an HTTP call to the
other module's own route. Each direction is a plain, targeted Prisma write:

- **Payroll Entry → Employee Registry**: `tx.employee.update({ data: { defaultEobiApplicable } })`,
  unconditional (the employee always exists — the entry's own FK guarantees it).
- **Employee Registry → current Draft entry**: `tx.payrollCycle.findFirst({ status: 'DRAFT' })` then
  `tx.payrollEntry.findUnique({ cycleId_employeeId })`; a no-op if no Draft cycle exists, no entry
  exists yet, or the entry is no longer editable (`released` or `payoutOutcome` set) — **never
  creates a PayrollEntry**, satisfying the explicit "do not create an incomplete/unintended entry"
  requirement. `Employee.defaultEobiApplicable` is retained regardless and is exactly what
  `createPayrollCycle`/`createPayrollEntry`/`syncEmployeeIntoCurrentDraftCycle` already copy onto a
  *newly created* entry, so the value is correctly used as the default the next time one is made.

Both directions are also genuine no-ops (no write, no audit entry) when the target's current value
already matches — an already-consistent pair produces zero churn, and there is no path from either
write back into this function, so an update loop is structurally impossible, not merely avoided by
convention.

**Historical safety.** The Employee→entry direction only ever looks up the *current* Draft cycle
(`status: 'DRAFT'`) — a Released or Archived cycle's entries are never reachable by that query, full
stop, not merely skipped by a secondary check. The entry-editability check
(`released`/`payoutOutcome`) additionally guards a Draft-cycle entry a Unit release sweep has already
resolved, even though its parent cycle hasn't been Finalized yet. Verified directly: a Released entry
(cycle still nominally Draft) is untouched by a later Employee Registry change; an Archived entry
(post-Finalize, post-rollover) is untouched, while the *new* Draft cycle's own carried-forward entry
for the same employee correctly *is* reached.

**Transactions.** Both writes for one logical change commit or roll back together, because both
happen inside the one transaction the primary edit already opens — proved with a real, reachable
forced failure (the sync's own audit-log call made to throw via `jest.spyOn`, not a mock of Prisma
itself), confirming neither the primary field nor the synced field persists, and neither audit entry
is written, when the second half fails.

**Permission analysis (investigated, not assumed).** `PATCH /employees/:id` requires
`employees:edit`; `PATCH /payroll-entries/:id` requires `payroll:entry` — two genuinely different
permission keys. The seeded `PAYROLL_STAFF` role happens to hold both today, but RBAC roles are
user-configurable, so a custom role could hold only one. Since a Draft-entry EOBI change now also
writes to Employee Registry (and vice versa), each service function now additionally requires the
*other* screen's permission **specifically when `eobiApplicable`/`defaultEobiApplicable` is part of
the request** — checked in the service layer (`currentUser.permissions.includes(...)`), not as a
blanket route-level change, so it never affects any other field on either route. A `payroll:entry`
holder without `employees:edit` gets a 403 attempting to change EOBI applicability via Payroll Entry
(their other financial-field edits are completely unaffected); symmetrically for
`employees:edit` without `payroll:entry` via Employee Registry. No existing permission was widened
or weakened — this is an additional, narrower requirement layered on top of the existing ones,
verified by two dedicated tests using bespoke single-permission roles (the real seeded roles can't
prove "lacks a permission," since `createTestUser` upserts them additively).

**Audit.** Two distinct actions, `employee.eobi_synced` and `payroll_entry.eobi_synced`, each
recorded only on the entity actually written, with `actorUserId`, `previousValue`, `newValue`,
`sourceScreen` (`'payroll_entry'`/`'employee_registry'`), and either the originating
`sourcePayrollEntryId` or the target `employeeId`/`cycleId` — never a second, duplicate-looking entry
for the same field on the same entity. The *primary* edit keeps using the exact audit mechanism that
route already had (`payroll_entry.updated`/`employee.updated`); only the *cascaded* write to the
other entity gets the new, distinctly-named action, so a reviewer can never mistake a synchronised
side effect for a direct user edit of that entity.

**Testing.** New file `backend/tests/eobi-bidirectional-sync.test.ts`, 13 tests covering all 12
requested scenarios (permission-bypass prevention split into 9a/9b, one per direction): both sync
directions, Released/Archived immunity (the latter also proving the *new* Draft cycle created by
rollover correctly receives the sync), the no-Draft-entry retention/later-default case, transaction
rollback under a forced failure, both permission-bypass directions, cross-screen refresh consistency,
unchanged `calcNet` deduction math, and release freezing the final value historically. One of this
session's own earlier tests (`payroll-entry-master-data-boundary.test.ts`'s EOBI test) asserted the
now-superseded "independent" behavior and was corrected, not merely relaxed, to assert the new
contract — with an explicit note explaining why the expectation changed.

**Results.** Backend: **1207/1208 tests passing** across 62 suites — the sole failure
(`corrections-service.test.ts`'s "Concurrent approval... two different requests... serialize" test)
is a pre-existing timing-sensitive race test, confirmed via `git diff` to be in a module this session
never touched, and confirmed to pass cleanly every time when run in isolation — the same category of
full-suite-only, sandbox-load-sensitive flakiness already on record elsewhere in this codebase, not a
regression. Frontend: **234/234 tests passing**, unaffected (this refinement is backend-service-layer
only; the Employee Registry and Payroll Entry EOBI checkboxes already existed and needed no frontend
change to pick up the new server-side behavior). Typecheck/lint/build all clean across shared/
backend/frontend, same two pre-existing unrelated issues already on record.

**Known limitation.** No live, same-session cross-screen UI update — the requirement was explicitly
"frontend refresh should show the same value in both locations" (satisfied: both screens' ordinary
GETs already reflect the synced DB state), not real-time cross-tab propagation without a refresh,
which was not implemented and not requested.

**No commit, push, or deployment occurred — do not mark this refinement complete** until reviewed.

### Phase 7D final refinement — EOBI Synchronisation Permissions & Audit — IMPLEMENTED, 2026-07-30, awaiting review, NOT COMMITTED

A same-day follow-up to the EOBI Bidirectional Synchronisation entry immediately above, which had
required the acting user to hold **both** `employees:edit` and `payroll:entry` before the
synchronised write would proceed. The client's own explicit instruction overrides that: the
synchronised write is an **internal system synchronisation**, not a second user edit, so only the
originating screen's own permission should ever be required.

**Permission model — before.** Changing `eobiApplicable` via `PATCH /payroll-entries/:id` required
`payroll:entry` (the route's own gate) **and** `employees:edit` (checked in the service layer,
specifically for this field), or a 403. Symmetrically, changing `defaultEobiApplicable` via
`PATCH /employees/:id` required `employees:edit` **and** `payroll:entry`, or a 403.

**Permission model — after.** Each route now requires only its own, pre-existing permission —
`payroll:entry` alone for Payroll Entry, `employees:edit` alone for Employee Registry. The
cross-permission checks (`payroll-entry.service.ts`'s `!currentUser.permissions.includes(EMPLOYEES_EDIT)`
throw, and `employees.service.ts`'s mirrored `!currentUser.permissions.includes(PAYROLL_ENTRY)` throw)
are deleted outright, not merely relaxed — `eobi-sync.service.ts`'s `syncEobiApplicability()` itself
never took a `currentUser` and never performed a permission check of its own; it only ever needed an
`actorUserId` to audit with, so removing the *callers'* extra checks required no change to the shared
function's own contract.

**This is not a permission bypass, verified explicitly.** The distinction the client drew — "the user
is authorised only to edit the originating resource; the second write exists solely to preserve data
consistency" — is exactly what the tests below prove: a `payroll:entry`-only user can change
`eobiApplicable` via Payroll Entry (and the sync to Employee Registry happens, performed by the
backend, not by that user editing Employee Registry themselves), but that same user still gets a 403
attempting to `PATCH /employees/:id` directly, for *any* field, EOBI or otherwise — the route's own
`employees:edit` gate is completely untouched. Symmetrically for an `employees:edit`-only user against
`PATCH /payroll-entries/:id`. Both directions were re-verified with bespoke single-permission test
roles (new tests 9c/9d, alongside the updated 9a/9b that now assert *success*, not rejection).

**Audit — before.** Two distinct, synchronisation-specific action names: `employee.eobi_synced` and
`payroll_entry.eobi_synced`, each recorded only on the *cascaded* entity (the one the direct edit
wasn't made to); the *directly-edited* entity's own change was folded into the ordinary generic
bundle (`payroll_entry.updated`/`employee.updated`), indistinguishable from any other field edit.

**Audit — after.** One consistent action per entity, regardless of which screen originated the
change: `employee.eobi_updated` and `payroll_entry.eobi_updated`, each carrying
`metadata: { previousValue, newValue, origin }` where `origin` is `'employee_registry'` or
`'payroll_entry'` — identifying which screen triggered the operation, whether *this* entity was the
one directly edited or the one synchronised as a result. `eobiApplicable`/`defaultEobiApplicable` are
now excluded from the generic `payroll_entry.updated`/`employee.updated` changes bundle (the same
`omitKeys` exclusion convention `employees.service.ts` already used for `siteId`/`unitId` ahead of
its own dedicated `employee.transferred` entry) — every EOBI applicability change, on either entity,
produces **exactly one** `*.eobi_updated` entry for that entity, never zero (folded silently into a
generic bundle) and never two (a generic entry plus a duplicate dedicated one). A single logical
change (e.g. toggling the Draft-entry checkbox) now writes exactly two audit rows total — one
`payroll_entry.eobi_updated` (origin: `payroll_entry`) on the entry actually edited, one
`employee.eobi_updated` (origin: `payroll_entry`) on the synchronised employee — both clearly
attributable to the same operation via the shared `origin` tag, never duplicate or misleading.

**Transaction behaviour — unchanged.** Both writes (and both new dedicated audit entries) still
happen inside the one transaction the primary edit already opens; `syncEobiApplicability()` is still
called exactly once, from inside that same transaction, by each of `updatePayrollEntry`/
`updateEmployee` — no recursive service/route calls, no frontend request chaining. Re-verified with
the same forced-failure technique as before (the sync's own audit write made to throw), now updated
to check for the renamed action (`employee.eobi_updated`) and to additionally confirm the
*originating* entity's own new `*.eobi_updated` entry (written moments earlier, same transaction)
also fails to persist — proving the whole operation, not just the counterpart write, rolls back
atomically.

**Testing.** `backend/tests/eobi-bidirectional-sync.test.ts` rewritten: 15 tests (up from 13) —
tests 1–8 and 10–12 keep their original scenarios with updated audit assertions (action names,
`origin` metadata, and explicit checks that both the directly-edited and synchronised entities each
get their own `*.eobi_updated` entry); the permission section is now four tests instead of two —
9a/9b now assert that a single-permission user *succeeds* (the corrected desired behaviour) while
also confirming the counterpart entity's sync and its audit `origin`, and new 9c/9d confirm the
*opposite* route (any field, not just EOBI) remains fully blocked for a user lacking that route's own
permission, directly proving the "not a bypass" distinction.

**Results.** Backend: **62 suites / 1210 tests, all passing** on this run — the `corrections-service.test.ts`
concurrency-timing test that flaked intermittently under full-suite load in the prior two entries'
runs (a pre-existing, `git diff`-confirmed-unrelated race test, in a module this revision never
touched) did not flake this run, consistent with load-dependent, not deterministic, flakiness.
`eobi-bidirectional-sync.test.ts` itself: 15/15. Typecheck/lint/build clean across shared/backend
(frontend unaffected — no frontend file touched by this revision either), same two pre-existing,
unrelated lint errors already on record.

**No commit, push, or deployment occurred — do not mark this refinement complete** until reviewed.

**Investigation only — no code, schema, or database change; no commit.** Requested and labeled
"Phase 8A" by its own out-of-band requester; belongs to this roadmap's **Phase 7** Reports sub-scope
(see §2's Phase 7 row for the naming clarification — this is unrelated to this table's own Phase 8,
Team Collaboration/Audit Log viewer).

Audited the actual existing architecture (Prisma schema, backend modules, frontend components,
export/print infrastructure, RBAC) rather than assuming what a Reports module needs, and produced a
full investigation report covering: authoritative reporting data sources; historical-data semantics
(the key finding — `PayrollEntry` is only partially snapshotted, and Bank Sheet's own "Account Title"
column already, knowingly, reads live `Employee.name` even for archived cycles); a recommended report
catalogue (Payroll Summary, Employee Payroll History, Project Site Payroll Report, Deduction Report,
Overtime Report, Advance Recovery Report, Salary Release Report, and a Variance/Month-on-Month report
flagged as needing explicit transfer/hire/departure handling before it can be trusted); a filter
matrix; drill-down architecture (Reports as a lens over existing screens, never a new detail-view
surface); export/print recommendations (reuse `exceljs`/`csv-stringify`/Puppeteer/`PrintButton`, no
new library); a performance/query strategy (flagging the absence of any generic server-side
pagination component as a real scaling gap); a permission recommendation (reuse the existing,
seeded-but-unused `reports:view`, no new permission); financial-correctness rules; and a full test
strategy. Delivered as a published Markdown artifact for the requester's own reference. STOP condition
honored — no implementation began in this investigation.

## Phase 8B Checkpoint 1 — Post-deployment Print Usability Refinement (2026-08-03)

**IMPLEMENTED, awaiting review, NOT COMMITTED.** Production UAT on the deployed Payroll Summary
report found a real usability defect: the on-screen report and Excel export were correct, but the
printed report was illegible — the full site-level table's 19 columns (Project Site plus 18
mostly-financial figures) meant headings and monetary values were truncated and squashed. Financial
calculations, CSV/XLSX behavior, and every other report/Dashboard remained explicitly out of scope
for this refinement.

**Fix**: configurable print fields for Payroll Summary only. Clicking Print now opens a
`PayrollSummaryPrintOptionsDialog` (`frontend/src/components/reports/`) before the browser's native
print dialog — individual checkboxes for the 8 existing summary cards and all 19 table columns
(stable `PayrollSummaryFigures`-keyed field ids, never display-label keys; Project Site locked,
always selected), three named presets (Compact Summary, Deductions, Release Status) each selecting a
paired card+column set, Select All / Clear Optional Fields / Reset to Default, a non-blocking
wide-selection warning (>10 columns) and a hard block against printing with no meaningful column
selected. Confirming calls the exact same shared `useTriggerPrint` engine every other print-enabled
page already uses (fixed to landscape/fit-to-page for this report, mirroring the `flushSync`
close-then-print sequencing the Production Print Defect fix already established) — no new print
engine. A `hidden print:block` cards/table block (mirroring Payroll Entry's own dedicated
print-only-markup pattern) renders only the selected fields, reading them directly from the same
already-loaded `PayrollSummaryReport` the on-screen table and CSV/XLSX exports already use — no new
fetch, no recalculated figure. The on-screen table (now separately `print:hidden`) still always
shows all 19 columns, unchanged; CSV/XLSX still always export the complete filtered report via the
same unaffected backend endpoints. Legibility comes from letting a smaller, user-chosen column set
size itself naturally (`table-layout: auto`, no forced shrink) rather than the shared `.print-fit`
class's existing `table-layout: fixed`/8.5px-font behavior, which is what made the full table
illegible in the first place and was deliberately not reused here. The user's last-used
preset/selection is remembered in browser `localStorage` only (`payroll-summary-print-fields:v1`) —
not persisted to PostgreSQL this checkpoint, per its own explicit scope. Full architecture write-up:
`docs/architecture/print-architecture.md`'s own "Payroll Summary — field-selectable print" section.

**Verification**: full frontend suite 278/278 passing (256 + 22 new: 15 dialog-component tests,
7 page-level tests covering the dialog-first Print flow, selected-field print rendering, on-screen/
export non-interference, and local-preference restoration). New real-Chromium Playwright coverage
(`tests/e2e/specs/17-reports.spec.ts`, 8/8 passing including the 2 pre-existing Reports tests):
Compact Summary/Deductions/Release Status/a custom selection each print exactly their own headings
(exact accessible-name match, so a truncated/ellipsized heading would fail even if some text node

printable container, no individual header cell is internally clipped, and no two adjacent
totals-row cells overlap; the on-screen table still shows every column under real screen media;

frontend presentation).

field-selectable print" section plus a Testing addendum), `docs/architecture/workflows/reports.md`

## Phase 7F — Payroll Workflow Integrity (2026-08-04)

**Naming note**: "Phase 7F" is this checkpoint's own out-of-band requester label, not this
roadmap's numbering — same convention already on record for "Phase 7D"/"Phase 8A"/"Phase 8B" in
earlier addenda. The actual work spans this roadmap's Phase 4 (Salary Release), Phase 3 (Payroll
Entry), and Phase 2 (Employee Registry) areas. **Phase 7D ("Master Data Boundary," 2026-07-30) is
referenced throughout below as this checkpoint's own direct predecessor — it was never written up
in this file at the time; a documentation gap this entry does not attempt to retroactively fill
beyond what's needed to explain what Phase 7F itself changed.**

Four objectives, all implemented, tested, and documented; **NOT committed, NOT pushed, NOT
deployed — stopped deliberately for review, per explicit instruction.**

### Objective 1 — Employee Registry as the authoritative Draft master-data source

Production UAT found a real defect: editing Gross Salary in Employee Registry did not update an
already-created, unreleased Payroll Entry. Investigation of the full Draft Payroll lifecycle found
Phase 7D's own "Master Data Boundary" live-overlay (`withLiveMasterData`,
`payroll-entry.service.ts`) and release-time freeze (`liveMasterByEntryId`,
`payroll-release.service.ts`) already covered `designation`/`bankId`/`branchCode`/`accountNumber`/
`iban` — `grossPay`, `employeeNameSnapshot`, and `fatherNameSnapshot` were the three fields that
pass missed. Fixed by extending both mechanisms to all three: a Draft entry now always reflects
Employee Registry's *live* value for Gross Salary/Name/Father Name (display **and** Net Salary
calculation, via `computeEntryCalc`), removed from `updatePayrollEntrySchema`/
`mapUpdateInputToEntryData` (PATCH silently strips them, same convention as the Phase 7D fields),
and frozen from Employee Registry's *current* record at the moment of release (or its own
Late/Straggler Sweep, Objective 3) rather than whatever the entry happened to be bootstrapped or
last edited with. CNIC/Employee Code were confirmed already correct — never independently stored
on `PayrollEntry`, always a live join — nothing to fix, only to verify. EOBI default applicability
confirmed already correct via its own, deliberately different bidirectional-sync mechanism
(`eobi-sync.service.ts`, Phase 7D) — `eobiApplicable` stays a genuine Payroll Entry toggle kept in
sync with `Employee.defaultEobiApplicable`, not a read-time overlay; `eobiAmount` (the deduction
figure) remains entirely Payroll-owned, untouched. Every Payroll-owned field (Worked Days, Work
Lines, Overtime, Leave, Allowances, Advance/Eid Advance Deduction, Fines, Hold, Remarks, Manual
EOBI Amount, Sort Order, Payout Outcome, Corrections, Balance Adjustments) confirmed to remain
exactly as Draft-editable as before — verified by a dedicated regression test asserting the PATCH
payload still applies every one of them, with `grossPay` removed from that same payload/assertion.
Historical immutability verified explicitly: a released/archived entry's frozen columns never
change when Employee Registry changes afterward (the same `released || payoutOutcome !== null`
guard `withLiveMasterData` already used for the Phase 7D fields).

**Known, documented limitation, not fixed**: Payroll Entry CSV/Excel export
(`payroll-entry-import-export.service.ts`) and Backup Package generation (which reuses it) both
read the entry's own stored column directly, bypassing the live overlay — mirrors a pre-existing,
already-shipped, deliberately out-of-scope gap in Bank Sheet's own "Account Title" (Phase 8A
Reports investigation). Left as a known limitation; fixing it touches export/backup infrastructure
beyond this checkpoint's Payroll Entry/Salary Release scope. Bank Sheets/Cash Receiving themselves
are unaffected by this gap — both are scoped to `released: true` entries only, which are always the
correctly-frozen, immutable snapshot regardless.

**Files**: `backend/src/modules/payroll-entry/payroll-entry.service.ts`,
`backend/src/modules/payroll-release/payroll-release.service.ts`,
`shared/src/schemas/payroll-entry.ts`, `frontend/src/components/payroll-entry/payroll-entry-row.tsx`,
`columns.ts`, `calc-input.ts`, `frontend/src/hooks/use-payroll-entry-editor.ts`.

**Tests**: new `backend/tests/payroll-entry-master-data-boundary-grosspay.test.ts` (6 tests — live
Gross Salary sync + Net Salary recalculation, live Name/Father Name sync, CNIC/Employee Code
already-live confirmation, PATCH-is-silently-ignored, release-time freeze from the *current*
Employee record, released-entry immunity); three pre-existing tests updated for the intentional
behavior change (`grossPay` no longer Draft-editable) — `payroll-entry-master-data-boundary.test.ts`,
`payroll-cycle.test.ts` (the grossPay carry-forward test re-scoped to what's still genuinely
Payroll-owned: EOBI/cycleDays/otRate), `payroll-cycle-archived-lock.test.ts`,
`payroll-cycle-rollover.test.ts` (both swapped to a still-editable field, `allowance`/`fine`, since
their own actual concern — editability-after-Finalize, Backup Package freshness — was never about
`grossPay` specifically); two frontend test files updated the same way
(`master-data-boundary.test.tsx`, `use-payroll-entry-editor.test.tsx`).

### Objective 2 — Release All

New bulk release action, scoped to one Project Site or "All Sites" (every Site the caller can
access — every Site for a Master Admin, exactly the caller's own assigned Sites otherwise, never
wider than the existing Site filter's own RBAC scope). Backend: `releaseAllEligible`
(`payroll-release.service.ts`), a new `POST /api/v1/payroll-cycles/:cycleId/units/release-all`
route. **Introduces no second release mechanism** — loops the exact same, unmodified
`releaseProjectUnit` once per not-yet-released Unit in scope, so every existing guarantee (lock
ordering, per-outcome master-data freeze, duplicate-identity blocking, correction/advance
settlement, audit trail) applies identically to a Release All-triggered release as to a manual one.

**Transaction strategy — one transaction per Project Unit, sequential, never one giant transaction,
never one per employee** (full reasoning in the function's own doc comment and
`docs/architecture/workflows/payroll-lifecycle.md`): a single transaction spanning the whole scope
risks exceeding the platform's transaction timeout at scale, holds the cycle-level lock for the
entire sweep's duration (blocking every concurrent edit/release against the cycle), and would roll
back every already-processed Unit if any single Unit anywhere in scope failed. Per-Unit reuses the
already-proven transaction boundary, bounds blast radius to one Unit's own headcount, and means one
Unit's genuine failure never touches another Unit's already-committed result — the loop catches
each Unit's own outcome independently and continues. Concurrency is a non-factor for parallelizing
Units instead: every `releaseProjectUnit` call already takes the cycle-level lock first, so
concurrent Unit releases against the same cycle already fully serialize at the database level.

Eligibility skips (Already Released, Hold, Recovery Due/No Payout already resolved) are enforced by
reusing `releaseProjectUnit`'s own existing candidate query and eligibility function — no
duplicated logic. Summary reports `releasedEntryCount` / `noPayDueCount` / `recoveryDueCount` /
`blockedCount` (+ `blockedEntries`, each tagged with its own Unit/Site) / `heldEntryCount`
(informational, computed once upfront — Held entries never move during the sweep) /
`unitsReleased` / `unitsAlreadyReleased` / `unitsFailed` (+ `failedUnits`, each with its own error)
— presented in the UI as "N Released / N Held / N Recovery Due / N No Payout / N Failed," matching
the requested wording. A genuine per-Unit technical failure is reported and skipped without
rolling back or blocking any other, already-succeeded Unit in the same call — verified by a test
that forces one specific Unit's own lookup to throw, confirming the other Units still commit and
the failed Unit can be retried cleanly afterward.

**Files**: `backend/src/modules/payroll-release/payroll-release.service.ts`,
`payroll-release.routes.ts`, `shared/src/schemas/payroll-release.ts`,
`frontend/src/hooks/use-payroll-release.ts`, `frontend/src/routes/salary-release-page.tsx`.

**Tests**: new `backend/tests/payroll-release-all.test.ts` (13 tests — Single Site, All Sites,
non-Master-User "All Sites" RBAC scoping, skip Hold, skip already-Released (idempotent re-call),
skip already-resolved No Payout/Recovery Due, partial success (one Unit already released
concurrently), rollback isolation (one Unit's genuine technical failure, verified not to affect or
roll back the others, then retried successfully), blocked-entry aggregation across Units/Sites,
RBAC rejection, non-Draft-cycle rejection, empty-scope well-formed zero result).

### Objective 3 — Hold Workflow Verification

Full audit of the documented lifecycle (Draft → Hold OFF → releasable → Hold ON → excluded →
release remaining → Site status → later Hold OFF → releasable again → only that employee releases
→ Site status updates correctly). The mechanics were already correct through "release remaining" —
`releaseProjectUnit`'s candidate query already excludes `hold: true`, and a held entry stays
ordinarily editable right up until it locks (`assertEntryEditable`). Two real gaps found and fixed:

1. **`getUnitReleaseStatus`'s `willReleaseCount` included Held entries** — never excluded them,
   overstating "will release now" in the Release confirmation dialog. Fixed to match
   `releaseProjectUnit`'s own candidate query exactly; a new `heldCount` field surfaces the
   excluded count explicitly rather than folding it silently into "remain pending." The
   confirmation dialog and per-Unit table both now show Held separately from "split across other
   Units," with distinct, accurate copy for each reason.
2. **The final documented step — un-Hold *after* the Unit already released — had no path back to
   release at all.** `releaseProjectUnit` unconditionally rejected a second call against an
   already-released Unit with a 409, regardless of whether anything had since become newly
   eligible; this is the "Late Entry" gap every prior checkpoint's own doc comments documented as
   explicitly deferred. Closed as a **Late/Straggler Sweep**: a second call against an
   already-released Unit is now accepted specifically when there's a newly-eligible straggler (no
   new `PayrollUnitRelease` row is written — still insert-once, still no "un-release," Principle
   9), and still rejected with the identical 409 when there genuinely isn't anything new — verified
   this doesn't regress the existing "double-click" 409 test, and doesn't prematurely resolve a
   straggler still waiting on a *different*, still-unreleased Unit (the same multi-Unit wait rule
   a fresh release already enforces). A dedicated `payroll_unit.late_sweep` audit entry,
   tagged with the original release's own id, distinguishes it from the original event in history.
   The Salary Release page surfaces this as a distinctly-labeled "Release Remaining" action
   (`willReleaseCount > 0` now correctly reappears even on an already-Released Unit).
   `getUnitReleaseStatus`'s own `willReleaseCount` computation needed the matching fix (it was
   hard-zeroed for any already-released Unit) for the action to ever become visible again.
   **Release All does not itself proactively hunt for late-sweep stragglers among already-released
   Units** — a deliberate, documented scope boundary; the per-Unit "Release Remaining" action
   covers the documented scenario.

**Files**: `backend/src/modules/payroll-release/payroll-release.service.ts`,
`frontend/src/hooks/use-payroll-release.ts`, `frontend/src/routes/salary-release-page.tsx`.

**Tests**: new `backend/tests/payroll-hold-workflow.test.ts` (4 tests — the full documented
lifecycle end to end including two full release cycles and an audit-trail assertion; the
Late/Straggler Sweep's own "nothing new eligible" 409 non-regression; a split-across-two-Units
straggler correctly waiting for its second Unit before a late sweep can resolve it; Site status
derivation across the whole lifecycle: Draft → fully released with a residual Held entry →
straggler resolved → fully released with nothing outstanding).

Investigation found no Site-level release status existed anywhere before this checkpoint — only

nothing stored (Principle 5). The per-Unit table remains the authoritative detail view; the badge
is a summary, shown next to the existing Cycle status badge.

## Phase 7G — CI Stability Remediation (2026-08-04)

Phase 7F's PR #6 was blocked by a CI failure in `payroll-hold-workflow.test.ts`'s "Release
Remaining idempotency" test — a Payslip PDF route returning 500. Investigation found two concrete,
in-scope defects, both fixed and committed:

1. `payroll-hold-workflow.test.ts` rendered real Puppeteer PDFs but never called `closeBrowser()`
   in its own `afterAll`, unlike every other real-Puppeteer suite — confirmed directly to leave a
   live, `ESTABLISHED` Chrome DevTools-Protocol WebSocket open after all 5 tests had already passed,
   which is why Jest never exited on its own afterward. Fixed: `afterAll` now closes the browser in
   a `finally`, matching the established pattern. Commit `cd71b5d`.
2. `backend/src/lib/logger.ts` silences all logs when `NODE_ENV=test`, so the real exception behind
   a PDF-route 500 was invisible in CI — grepping a full CI log for an actual occurrence found no
   trace of it. Fixed with one narrow, additive diagnostic in `render-pdf.ts`: when
   `renderHtmlToPdf`'s one built-in retry is also exhausted, a single structured `console.error`
   (already allowed by `no-console`) reports the error's own name/message/stack — never the
   rendered HTML or PDF options, which can carry real payroll data — only in `NODE_ENV=test`, never
   touching the shared logger's own config. Commit `15a3776`.

This immediately paid off: the very next CI run reproduced the PDF failure again, and the new
diagnostic captured the real exception for the first time — `"Error: Test environment has been torn
down"` — a Jest/VM-lifecycle signature, not a payroll defect. That finding is what Phase 7H (below)
investigates and fixes. PR #6 remained blocked, unmerged, per this checkpoint's own explicit
instruction not to guess or re-run indefinitely.

## Phase 7H — Permanent PDF Test Infrastructure Stabilisation (2026-08-04)

**Objective**: resolve the `"Test environment has been torn down"` failure Phase 7G's diagnostic
surfaced, permanently, and unblock PR #6. Investigation-first, per explicit instruction — no
architecture chosen before empirical reproduction.

### Root cause (proven, not inferred)

A minimal reproduction matrix was built for five call paths (direct `renderHtmlToPdf()`, the
`renderPayslipPdfBuffer()` service call, the real HTTP route via supertest, a standalone
`node`/`tsx` script outside Jest entirely, and a child process spawned from a Jest test):

- **Outside Jest** (standalone `tsx` script, 20 real renders): **20/20 succeeded**, every time —
  the production render pipeline itself was never the problem.
- **Direct in-Jest calls, run alongside many sibling files under `--runInBand`** (40 throwaway test
  files, each independently calling `renderHtmlToPdf()`): **37/40 and 18/20 failed** across two
  stress runs, always with the identical stack trace — through `jest-util`'s own `invariant()`,
  called from inside the `eval`'d dynamic `import('puppeteer')` at `browser.ts`'s documented
  ESM-interop workaround, inside `launchBrowser()`. Never application code.
- **A child process spawned from a Jest test, given the same work, under the identical concurrent
  stress**: **10/10 succeeded**.

Mechanism: `browser.ts`'s `new Function('return import("puppeteer")')` (required because Puppeteer
22+ ships ESM-only against this backend's CommonJS compile target — see that file's own existing
comment) is a genuine, sometimes-slow native Node operation. Jest's `--experimental-vm-modules`
mode gives every test *file* its own disposable VM realm, torn down independently once that file's
tests finish. Under real concurrent load (many files each racing through this same dynamic import
around the same time), the import can resolve *after* Jest has already torn down the realm that
started it — a scheduling race on Jest's own side, not a missing `await` in application code (the
full `renderHtmlToPdf → renderOnce → getBrowser` chain was re-verified, correctly awaited
top-to-bottom). `--experimental-vm-modules` cannot be removed without breaking Puppeteer loading
entirely (it's what makes the ESM-interop workaround reach Node's real loader at all), so no
config-level fix was viable — confirming an architectural fix was required.

### Architecture chosen: persistent PDF test worker (Option B)

A dedicated child process (`backend/src/lib/pdf/worker/`) that is never itself inside a Jest VM
realm — structurally immune to the race, not merely less likely to hit it. `render-pdf.ts`'s
`renderHtmlToPdf()` delegates to it whenever `NODE_ENV=test` (every Jest run, local and CI);
`development`/`production` are completely unchanged. The worker imports and calls the exact same
`renderOnce()`/`browser.ts` code Jest's own real-Puppeteer suites already used, not a
reimplementation — production rendering output is identical either way. Full design, ownership/
cleanup model, and observability strategy: `docs/architecture/testing.md`'s "Backend PDF test
architecture" section.

**Two real bugs found and fixed while stress-testing this architecture itself** (both about Chrome
specifically outliving the process meant to own it, confirmed directly via `ps -eo pid,ppid,pgid`):
a duplicate-spawn race (the client's own liveness check could false-negative under load, letting a
second worker steal the socket from a healthy first one — fixed by making the worker's own startup
bind-first and reserve the liveness check for a genuine `EADDRINUSE`), and an orphaned-Chrome leak
(Puppeteer launches Chrome detached into its **own** OS process group, separate from the worker's —
so `browser.close()` not fully terminating every Chrome helper process left true orphans with
nothing left to clean them up; fixed with a tracked-pid backstop kill on shutdown/recycle, plus a
sweep for any orphan left by a hard-killed previous worker generation on the next spawn).

### Verification

Each real-Puppeteer suite in isolation ×5, all real-PDF suites together ×5, full backend suite ×3
(3,843 total test executions across the three full runs): **zero
`"Test environment has been torn down"` occurrences, zero lingering Chrome/CDP/worker processes
after any run.** The one failure across all of this repetition was `corrections-service.test.ts`'s
already-documented, unrelated concurrency-timing flake (see that file's own history above) —
confirmed unrelated to PDF rendering and not misclassified as one. The query-count flake (KI-10,
`docs/release/KNOWN_ISSUES_v1.0.md`) did not recur in this checkpoint's runs; it is unchanged and
still open — not touched, per explicit instruction not to weaken it.

### Files

New: `backend/src/lib/pdf/worker/{protocol,pdf-worker.entry,pdf-worker-client}.ts`,
`backend/src/lib/pdf/normalize-error.ts`, `backend/tests/globalTeardown.ts`,
`backend/tests/pdf-worker-infrastructure.test.ts`, `backend/tests/pdf-worker-timeout.test.ts`.
Modified: `backend/src/lib/pdf/render-pdf.ts` (worker delegation, stage tracking, retry logic
extracted into `renderWithOneRetry` for direct testability), `backend/src/lib/pdf/browser.ts`
(added `peekBrowserProcessPid()` — read-only introspection only, no behavior change),
`backend/jest.config.js` (`globalTeardown`), `backend/tests/{payslips,statements,
payroll-hold-workflow}.test.ts` (`closeBrowser()` → `closePdfRenderer()`, since rendering now
happens in the shared worker, not each file's own in-process singleton),
`backend/tests/pdf-render-diagnostics.test.ts` (rewritten against the extracted
`renderWithOneRetry`, since the public `renderHtmlToPdf` now delegates to the worker in
`NODE_ENV=test` and can no longer be unit-tested by mocking `browser.ts` directly). No payroll
business logic, Reports, or Dashboard code touched.

### Regression / Testing

Typecheck, lint, backend build, frontend build all clean. Full detail and exact counts in the
"Backend PDF test architecture" section referenced above.

**No commit yet as of this entry — see below for the commit SHAs once applied.** No merge,

**A real bug found and fixed during test-writing, not shipped**: several detail-endpoint fields
(`BalanceAdjustment.amount`/`.remainingAmount`, settlement `amountApplied`, `CorrectionPayment.amount`,
Advance `totalAmount`/`outstandingBalance`/`deductionThisEntry`, Correction `oldNetSalary`/
`newNetSalary`, and every field in the detail `calculation` block not already routed through
`calcNet`) were built with a bare `Decimal.toString()` instead of `.toFixed(2)` — empirically
confirmed via a direct Postgres round-trip that `toString()` silently drops trailing zeros
(`2000.00` → `"2000"`), while every other monetary value in this codebase that reaches an API
response is either funneled through `calcNet`'s own internal `.toFixed(2)` or explicitly calls it
directly. Caught by the test suite's own exact-string assertions (`'2000.00'` expected, `'2000'`
received) before this reached the completion report, not after. Fixed at every call site; no

## Post-Checkpoint-1A UAT Stabilization — Sticky Header Containment, EOBI Totals/Bulk Apply, Project Site Form Reset — IMPLEMENTED, 2026-08-05, awaiting review, NOT COMMITTED

Three independently-reported UAT defects, fixed as one scoped checkpoint per explicit instruction —
no Employee Payroll History Checkpoint 1B, Dashboard, or other report work was started. Full
before/after verification (real Postgres, real backend, real Chromium via Playwright) is recorded
in this session's own completion report; this entry records what was built and the root cause each
fix addresses.

**Part A — Sticky header containment.** **Wording correction (independent review, 2026-08-05,
applied to this entry and to `docs/design-system.md`'s matching rule — historical record below
preserved unchanged):** "Root cause" here should be read as *a confirmed robustness gap*, isolated
by direct pixel sampling — not as a proven root cause of the specific reported "blank strip while
scrolling" symptom itself, which was never reproduced conclusively in the review environment (the
paragraph's own next sentence already records that the "bleed-through" hypothesis was directly
disproven, and no live/active-scroll transient artifact was ever captured — only static, settled
screenshots). Fully opaque rows are a structurally sound fix regardless: they prevent any
underlying content from becoming visible during sticky/virtualized composition, by construction.
Isolated by direct pixel sampling of a
headless-Chromium screenshot (not guessed): every virtualized Payroll Entry row
(`payroll-entry-row.tsx`) had a fully **transparent** background
(`background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0)`), relying entirely on the ancestor Card's own incidental white
surface rather than painting its own opaque one — a real robustness gap for content sharing screen
space with the grid's sticky group-header/column-header/totals rows during scroll compositing.
Investigation also directly disproved several other hypotheses before landing on this one: the app
shell's document-never-scrolls architecture (`app-shell.tsx`'s `h-screen overflow-hidden`) was
confirmed intact via live `window.scrollY`/`document.documentElement.scrollHeight` measurement; the
shared `Topbar`'s own `sticky` class was confirmed inert-but-harmless (it sits outside `<main>`, the
sole scroll owner, as a flex sibling — never actually needs to stick); and the grid's own two-tier
sticky header (`bg-surface`, `z-20`) was confirmed to correctly occlude scrolled-past content once
its own label text was correctly distinguished from a hypothesized "bleed-through." **Fix**: an
explicit `bg-surface-2` on every row's own root element (`payroll-entry-row.tsx`) — the smallest,
most directly-justified change, since this is the one place in the whole app with a genuine
sticky-header + GPU-transformed-virtualized-content combination (`docs/design-system.md`'s own
documented exemption for this grid). **App-wide audit** (Dashboard, Salary Release, Bank Sheet, Cash
Receiving, Advances, Payslips, Corrections, Employee Registry, Reports, Project Sites, Project
Units, Users, Settings, Statements, Tasks): direct repository search confirmed no other page has
any sticky element of its own at all — the shared `Card`/`CardHeader`/`<Table>` primitives (used
identically everywhere) carry no sticky positioning, so there was no second implementation to patch
and no page-specific transparent override to find. Spot-verified live (Employee Registry, Reports,
Project Sites, Users) — document never scrolls, topbar stays opaque, both before and after
scrolling `<main>`.

**Part B — EOBI effective-deduction total.** Confirmed defect: the Payroll Entry footer's EOBI
Amount column summed every row's **raw configured** `eobiAmount` (`LiveTotalsStore`'s own
`eobiAmount` field, fed by `payroll-entry-row.tsx`'s live-edit effect and `calc-input.ts`'s
`computeServerSnapshot`) regardless of `eobiApplicable` — a disabled employee's amount was still
counted. `calcNet` itself (`shared/src/lib/calc-net.ts`) was never wrong (already-passing tests
confirm `eobiDeduction = eobiApplicable ? eobiAmount : 0`); the bug was two frontend aggregation
paths bypassing it: the live-totals snapshot, and the Payroll Entry page's own print-totals/
print-table `deductions` calculation (`payroll-entry-page.tsx`, both the aggregate total and the
per-row printed Deductions cell), which independently re-summed `eobiAmount + advanceDeduction +
eidAdvanceDeduction + fine` by hand instead of using `calc.totalDeduction`. **Fix**: both snapshot
functions now store `eobiApplicable ? eobiAmount : 0` (never the raw amount) under that field;
`payroll-entry-row.tsx`'s live-edit effect also gained `effectiveEntry.eobiApplicable` to its own
dependency array — it was missing, so toggling Applicable alone (with no other field changing)
never re-reported the row to the totals store, meaning the footer would not update immediately on
toggle even before this fix's other change. Print totals/table now call `calcNet` once per entry
and read `calc.totalDeduction` directly, matching the on-screen grid path exactly (Principle 6).
No raw-`eobiAmount`-sum path was found anywhere else in the audit (Bank Sheets, Cash Receiving,
Payslips, Payroll Summary, Employee Payroll History, Corrections replay, and CSV/XLSX export were
all already correct, reading `calc.eobiDeduction`/`calcNet`'s output or, for export, the raw
per-row figure with no total column at all).

**Part C — Bulk EOBI Amount.** New `field: 'eobiAmount'` variant on the existing
`bulkUpdatePayrollEntriesSchema` discriminated union (`shared/src/schemas/payroll-entry.ts`) and the
existing `bulkUpdatePayrollEntries` service function (`payroll-entry.service.ts`) — reuses every
existing guarantee of that one shared code path rather than adding a second mechanism: mandatory
non-empty `siteIds`, `assertSiteAccess` per site, the same editable-row filter
(`released = false` and cycle not `ARCHIVED`), a single `payrollEntry.updateMany` bulk statement
(no per-row loop), one summary `payroll_entry.bulk_updated` audit entry (field/value/matchedCount/
appliedCount/siteIds), and `payroll:entry` permission. Applies to **every** matched entry regardless
of its own `eobiApplicable` — a disabled row still receives the new amount, ready for if/when
applicability is later enabled — and never touches `eobiApplicable` itself (on `PayrollEntry`) or
`Employee.defaultEobiApplicable` (verified directly in tests). Frontend: a fourth field added to
`CopyToAllToolbar` (`copy-to-all-toolbar.tsx`), labeled "EOBI Amount," reusing the exact same
Bulk-Apply-to-Filtered-Employees interaction, validation (`isValidDecimalDraft`), and success/error
toast pattern the three existing fields (Cycle Days/OT Rate/Leave Rate) already use — no new UI
pattern introduced. A successful apply invalidates the entries query, which refreshes both the grid
and the footer total with no full page reload.

**Part D — Project Site create-form reset.** Root cause: the *create*-mode `SiteFormModal`
(`project-sites-page.tsx`) was a single, unconditionally-mounted React component instance for the
whole life of the Project Sites page — only its `open` prop toggled. `useState(site?.name ?? '')`
(and the same for `unitLabel`/`address`) only ever evaluates its initializer on first mount, so
nothing ever reset those fields across a later close/reopen or after a successful create — exactly
the reported defect. The *edit*-mode usage never had this problem, since it was already
conditionally rendered (`{editingSite && <SiteFormModal site={editingSite} .../>}`) — selecting a
different site, or opening Create right after Edit, already always mounted a fresh instance seeded
from that specific site. **Fix**: create now follows the identical mount-fresh-every-time
discipline (`{createOpen && <SiteFormModal .../>}`), matching every other modal already in this
file (`ManageUnitsModal`, `DeleteSiteModal`). A new "Add another after this one" checkbox (`Checkbox`,
this codebase's one shared component) — the one case a remount alone can't cover, since it must
blank the *same* still-open instance rather than close it — calls an explicit `resetForm()` (back to
`{ name: '', unitLabel: 'Branch', address: '' }`, `'Branch'` being the schema's own documented
default, not an arbitrary blank) and refocuses the Site Name field. `SiteFormModal` is now exported
(previously module-private) purely for direct component-test coverage of this lifecycle, independent
of the page's own list/dropdown wiring. Every scenario in the reported defect was verified against
the real, running application (Playwright, real backend): create → Add another → blank; create →
close → reopen Create → blank; create → close → Edit an existing site → close → Create → blank;
close Create → Edit → real values load correctly; edit path never offers "Add another" (editing is
always about exactly one already-selected site).

**Tests added**: backend — `payroll-entry.test.ts`'s new `eobiAmount` describe block (mixed
applicable/non-applicable rows, site-scope, applicability/Employee-default untouched, audit record,
negative-amount rejection) and `payroll-entry-performance.test.ts`'s new 10,000-row Bulk EOBI Amount
timing case. Frontend — `calc-input.test.ts` (new file, `computeServerSnapshot`'s effective-deduction
rule), `payroll-entry-grid.test.tsx`'s two new describe blocks (opaque row/sticky-header background
assertions; footer total with disabled/enabled/mixed rows), `project-sites-page.test.tsx` (new file,
`SiteFormModal`'s full reset lifecycle, 5 tests). E2E — `06-ui-regression.spec.ts` extended with a
40-row Payroll Entry scroll/opacity assertion plus a 3-page (Employee Registry/Reports/Users)
document-never-scrolls sweep; new `18-post-checkpoint-1a-uat-stabilization.spec.ts` (EOBI mixed-row
footer + bulk apply + immediate-toggle-update; Project Site full create/Add-another/edit lifecycle).

**Verification**: backend full suite **1369/1369**; frontend full suite **325/325** (312 pre-existing
+ 13 new); `typecheck`/`lint`/`build` clean across `shared`/`backend`/`frontend`; `git diff --check`
clean; full Playwright suite result recorded in this session's own completion report. No schema
migration required (the bulk-update route already existed; only its accepted `field` union grew).

**Explicitly not started this checkpoint**: Employee Payroll History Checkpoint 1B (frontend),
Dashboard, and every other report remain exactly as scoped before this session — this checkpoint
touched only the three reported UAT defects.

### Post-Checkpoint-1A UAT Stabilization — Independent Review Remediation (M1–M4) — IMPLEMENTED, 2026-08-05, awaiting review, NOT COMMITTED

A separate, later session ran a rigorous, independent, read-only review of the checkpoint above —
re-deriving every claim from the actual diff and live application behavior rather than trusting the
original report — and returned **APPROVE WITH NON-BLOCKING NOTES**: zero Blockers, zero High
findings, five Medium findings (M1–M5), two Low findings. Full review record: this session's own
review report (root causes, exact evidence, every command run). Explicitly approved for remediation:
**M1–M4 only** — M5 (Corrections Scenario 4's own, pre-existing, unrelated reproducibility) is
deliberately left open, unrelated to this diff, tracked separately.

**M1 — documentation precision.** The wording correction described in Part A's own entry above
(the "Wording correction (independent review...)" paragraph) plus the matching correction in
`docs/design-system.md` §2.1 and this same clarifying cross-reference in `docs/SESSION_HANDOFF.md`
§31. No claim in any of the three files now asserts a *confirmed* causal link between the row-
transparency fix and the user's own specific reported screenshot — each is now explicit that the
robustness gap itself is confirmed, the reported symptom was never conclusively reproduced in the
review environment, and fully opaque rows are correct by construction regardless. The historical
investigation record (SESSION_HANDOFF §31's own paragraph, already accurate) is preserved verbatim.

**M2 — bulk audit previous-value summary.** `payroll-entry.service.ts`'s `bulkUpdatePayrollEntries`
now records a bounded, truthful `previousValues` field in the same `payroll_entry.bulk_updated`
audit metadata, generically for all four bulk fields (`leaveRate`/`otRate`/`cycleDays`/`eobiAmount`),
not only `eobiAmount`:

```
previousValues:
  { kind: 'single'; value: string | number | null }
  | { kind: 'mixed'; distinctCount: number; minimum: number; maximum: number }
```

`kind: 'single'` when every editable row already shared the same value (including a genuine `null`
for an unset `leaveRate`/`otRate`) — the value itself, verbatim. `kind: 'mixed'` otherwise, with a
distinct-value count and the numeric min/max across whichever rows had a value at all (a `null` row
still counts toward `distinctCount`, never toward min/max). Distinctness is compared numerically
(`Number(v)`), not by raw string, so e.g. a `Decimal` serializing as `"400"` on one row and `"400.00"`
on another is correctly recognized as the same value rather than inflating `distinctCount`. This is
a fixed-size summary regardless of how many rows matched — never one entry per employee, so it costs
nothing extra even at a 10,000-row match (re-measured: 780ms, unchanged from before this
remediation's own 714ms baseline, both comfortably inside the 2000ms target).

**The read that determines the matched/editable set and the previous values now runs *inside* the
same transaction as the `updateMany` and the audit insert** (previously a separate, pre-transaction
`prisma.payrollEntry.findMany`) — closes a genuine, if narrow, TOCTOU gap: without this, a
concurrent request could change a row's value in the window between the old non-transactional read
and this write, making the recorded "previous value" untruthful. Zero-match/zero-applied behavior is
unchanged — no write, no audit entry, no fabricated `previousValues` when nothing is editable.

**M3 — forced audit-failure rollback test.** New test in `backend/tests/payroll-entry.test.ts`'s
`eobiAmount` describe block, using the same `jest.spyOn(auditLogService, 'recordAuditLog')` pattern
already established in `eobi-bidirectional-sync.test.ts`: forces the bulk action's own summary audit
insert to fail, asserts the whole request 500s, and directly re-reads every affected row afterward —
every matched entry's `eobiAmount` and `version` are unchanged (no partial write survived), both
entries' `eobiApplicable` flags are unchanged, the out-of-scope site's entry is unchanged, both
employees' `Employee.defaultEobiApplicable` are unchanged, and no audit row for the attempted value
exists. A second new test (independent of the rollback one) proves the `previousValues` summary
itself is truthful: three entries seeded with three different starting amounts (300/400/450.50)
produce `{ kind: 'mixed', distinctCount: 3, minimum: 300, maximum: 450.5 }`, and a follow-up bulk
apply against the now-uniform population correctly reports `{ kind: 'single', value: '600' }` — the
summary reflects the *current* matched population on every call, never a stale record of an earlier
one. **4 new tests total** (2 previous-value/rollback tests here, described above; the pre-existing
2 `eobiAmount` tests from the original checkpoint are otherwise unchanged) —
`backend/tests/payroll-entry.test.ts`'s own suite is now 18/18.

**M4 — conflict-row opacity.** Root cause: `cn()` (built on `tailwind-merge`) resolves a `bg-*`
class conflict by keeping only the *last* class in the list — `payroll-entry-row.tsx`'s own
`status === 'conflict' && 'bg-danger-light/40'` (a 40%-opacity class) therefore silently **dropped**
the row's base `bg-surface-2` (M1's own opaque-row fix) whenever a row was in conflict status,
reintroducing the exact translucent-background gap that fix exists to close, for this one reachable
row state (a concurrent-edit version conflict during autosave). Fixed by dropping the `/40` opacity
suffix — `bg-danger-light` (no modifier) is the same solid, already-vetted semantic color
`badge.tsx`'s own `hold`/`red` variants and the Payroll Summary Print Options dialog's warning
banner already use at full opacity elsewhere in this app, so this introduces no new color, only
removes an accidental transparency. Verified directly against `tailwind-merge`'s own resolved
output (`node -e "twMerge(...)"`), not merely reasoned about: the fixed combination now resolves to
`bg-danger-light` with no opacity suffix, confirmed. **Test added**: new file
`payroll-entry-row.test.tsx` (2 tests) — mocks `usePayrollEntryEditor` to force `status: 'conflict'`
and asserts the row's real, rendered, tailwind-merge-resolved `className` both contains
`bg-danger-light` and matches no `bg-*/NN` opacity-suffixed pattern at all (the exact regression this
guards against); a companion test confirms an ordinary (non-conflict) row still resolves to the
plain `bg-surface-2`.

**Verification (this remediation pass)**: `backend/tests/payroll-entry.test.ts` **18/18** (4 new);
`backend/tests/payroll-entry-performance.test.ts`'s Bulk EOBI Amount case re-measured at 780ms/10,000
rows (unchanged from baseline); frontend full suite **327/327** (325 prior + 2 new in
`payroll-entry-row.test.tsx`); `typecheck`/`lint`/`build` clean across `shared`/`backend`/`frontend`
(0 errors; only the same pre-existing warning baseline as before — KI-4's 6 frontend warnings, the
same 10 unrelated backend-script warnings); `git diff --check` clean. Full backend suite result
recorded in `docs/SESSION_HANDOFF.md` §31's own follow-up addendum, honestly, whatever it shows —
per this remediation's own explicit instruction not to repeatedly rerun chasing a clean PDF-worker
result if the same already-documented KI-10-class failure recurs.

**Corrections Scenario 4 (M5) remains open, separate, and unresolved** — this remediation pass
deliberately did not touch Corrections, Statements, PDF infrastructure, Dashboard, or any module
outside the exact M1–M4 scope authorized. **Employee Payroll History Checkpoint 1B remains not
started.**

## Phase 7 Reports — Employee Payroll History, Checkpoint 1B (Frontend, Print, E2E, and Phase Close-Out) — IMPLEMENTED, 2026-08-05, awaiting review, NOT COMMITTED

Frontend-only, over the frozen Checkpoint 1A backend — no backend, shared-contract, or database
change in this checkpoint. Full design record: `docs/architecture/workflows/reports.md` §15.10 (new).
This entry records what was built and verified; §15.10 records the full detail.

**Routes and permission**: `/reports/employee-payroll-history` and
`/reports/employee-payroll-history/:entryId`, lazy-loaded, both gated on `PERMISSIONS.STATEMENTS_VIEW`
— never `reports:view` — via the existing `RequireSession`/`RequirePermission` pattern. The Reports
catalogue card (`reports-page.tsx`) gained an additive, optional per-entry `requiredPermission` field
(every other entry unaffected) so this card is hidden entirely, never a broken/unauthorized link, for
a user who lacks `statements:view` even though the catalogue page itself only requires `reports:view`.

**Data hooks and query behavior**: `hooks/use-employee-payroll-history.ts` imports every DTO directly
from `@payroll/shared` (already the single shared source of truth for this report, unlike Payroll
Summary's/Statements' own backend-internal types — importing rather than hand-copying avoids a
second, driftable copy of 15+ interfaces). List/detail/employee-lookup queries follow this codebase's
established conventions (plain array query keys, no `keepPreviousData`, pagination controls disabled
during refetch instead, filters/sort resetting page to 1, a 300ms-debounced employee search). The
export function is the first in this codebase to handle the backend's structured `413
EXPORT_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` response — a new `ExportRowLimitExceededError` surfaces the backend's own
message via `toast.error`, never a generic "export failed" and never a silent current-page fallback.

**Historical employee lookup**: `components/reports/employee-payroll-history-employee-lookup.tsx` — a
dedicated fork of `StatementEmployeeLookup`'s own interaction shape, pointed at the Checkpoint 1A
`GET /employee-payroll-history/employees` endpoint — never the current-site-scoped `EmployeeLookup`.

**Filters implemented** (the approved set only, per Step 5): Employee, Site (multi-select), Unit
(disabled unless exactly one Site is selected), Cycle From/Cycle To, Row Status, Has Correction, Has
Outstanding Origin Balance (both a new tri-state All/Yes/No select — no shared tri-state component
existed before this checkpoint; now documented as a reusable pattern, `docs/design-system.md` §2.4),
Current Roster Status. No standalone Date Range/Year/Month, no vague Release Status, no duplicate
Held checkbox. Clear Filters restores defaults while preserving the current sort.

**Table columns and sorting**: Payroll Month, Employee Code, Employee Name, Project Site, Primary
Unit (`+N more`), Designation, Total Earnings, Total Deductions, Net Salary, Row Status (5 distinct
badge tones, never derived client-side — a new colocated `employee-payroll-history-labels.ts`),
Corrections (count badge), Outstanding Origin Balance (a plain badge, never a financial figure),
Released Date, and a read-only "View Details" action. Only the six backend-approved sort fields are
sortable; sorting and pagination are both strictly server-driven (`ReportPagination`, no in-memory
slicing, no client-side sort).

**Totals behavior**: every summary card renders the backend's own `EmployeePayrollHistoryTotals`
verbatim; when `totalsComputed` is `false` (matching set beyond the 20,000-row ceiling), the three
monetary cards are replaced by an explanatory notice rather than a misleading zero, while the table
itself remains available. No client-side summation anywhere.

**Detail-page structure**: a dedicated route, never a modal, modeled on
`balance-adjustment-detail-page.tsx`. 9 top-level sections, with Settlements and Correction Payments
presented inline within the relevant correction/balance-adjustment sections rather than as
independent top-level cards, in the approved order (Identity & Historical
Assignment; Original Payroll Result, labeled "Corrections and later settlements do not overwrite this
original payroll result"; Work Line/Unit Breakdown; Release Information with a safe `{id, name}`
actor only; Linked Advances; Corrections Originating From This Entry, each with its own inline
Resulting Balance Adjustment and settlement history; Automatic Recovery Balance Adjustment kept
visually/textually distinct from a correction-originated one; Materializations Consumed By This
Entry, with explicit "Origin cycle: {X}" wording; Audit References, read-only, no broken link since
no Audit Log viewer route exists yet). CNIC renders; no banking field is ever present. A 404 renders
one plain "could not be found" message, never distinguishing nonexistent from inaccessible.

**Export behavior**: Export CSV/Export Excel, one page-level mutually-exclusive `activeExport` state
(shared with Print), current filters and sort always applied, never just the current page, a
structured 413 message shown via toast.

**Browser Print (Version 1 scope)**: a dedicated `EmployeePayrollHistoryPrintOptionsDialog` and fresh
field vocabulary (`employee-payroll-history-print-fields.ts`) — never a reuse of Payroll Summary's own
field ids. Prints the current paginated page only, never an unbounded fetch, never backend Puppeteer.
Defaults to every safe card/column selected (10 cards, 13 columns, Employee Name locked); a scaled-down
Print Readability indicator warns, never blocks, on a wide selection; persists to a report-specific
`localStorage` key (`employee-payroll-history-print-fields:v1`) only, never PostgreSQL. No CNIC, no
banking, no release actor, no drill-down section is ever offered as a print field. No backend PDF.

**Tests**: 62 new frontend tests — `use-employee-payroll-history.test.ts`,
`employee-payroll-history-labels.test.ts`, `employee-payroll-history-print-fields.test.ts`,
`reports-employee-payroll-history-page.test.tsx`, `reports-employee-payroll-history-detail-page.test.tsx`
(5 new colocated files), plus a new `reports-page.test.tsx` (3 tests) for the catalogue

`typecheck`/`lint`/`build` clean across `shared`/`backend`/`frontend`; `typecheck:e2e` clean;

**Performance observations** (measured during manual/Playwright verification, not a production SLA):
the list fetch always requests exactly one page; the employee lookup fires one debounced request per
distinct search term; opening the detail route issues exactly one detail request, never a per-row
prefetch; each filter/sort/pagination change produces exactly one new list request, no duplicate

**Known limitations, disclosed**: (1) this report only ever displays, never controls, the exact
settlement timing of a `DEFERRED PAYABLE` correction's materialized obligation — the Playwright suite

characteristic is unchanged and now also drives this page's own totals card on first paint; (3)
